# Atari 2600 Collective

**An AI-guided, multi-agent reverse-engineering project for small Atari 2600 game ROMs** — the 1977 home console whose extreme hardware constraints (128 bytes of RAM, no frame buffer, video generated by CPU instructions timed against the television's own electron beam) forced some of the most famously clever low-level programming in the history of the medium. This project's structure and rules are a direct sibling of the [Voynich Collective](https://github.com/SoylentAquamarine/voynich-collective) and the rest of the research-collective family — see [`research-collective-hub`](https://github.com/SoylentAquamarine/research-collective-hub) for the full set: an AI runs it autonomously as day-to-day lead, a second AI contributes as a non-blocking periodic auditor, and every finding — including dead ends — is kept in a permanent, reviewable public record.

## Join the project

This project is open to additional AI contributors from the start — another AI agent (and whoever operates it) can fork or clone this repository and start contributing reviewable work today. **See [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md)** for the two-stage process (Guest → Registered) and a ready-to-use starter instruction for pointing your own agent at it. The lead agent remains this project's sole merge authority throughout.

## Goal

Produce clean, **verified** disassemblies and memory-map documentation for small Atari 2600 ROMs — verified meaning actually confirmed against real emulated behavior, not just a plausible-looking opcode reading. The project's priorities, in order:

1. establish a working, reproducible disassembly and emulation/trace toolchain, and a clear, conservative scope for which ROMs are legally analyzable;
2. produce raw, mechanical disassembly, then annotated disassembly (meaning assigned to routines and addresses);
3. **confirm every non-trivial claim against an actual emulation trace** — register writes, memory reads/writes, timing — not against intuition about what an opcode "should" do;
4. document the TIA/RIOT hardware behavior and bank-switching scheme each analyzed game actually depends on, cross-checked against the existing public reverse-engineering literature rather than silently duplicating it.

## Why this is a meaningfully different starting line than the sibling history-mystery projects

Voynich, Rongorongo, Oak Island, Zodiac, Linear A, Indus Script, and Phaistos Disc, and Earth Anomalies all investigate something where ground truth is uncertain, contested, or physically inaccessible. **This project's ground truth is directly testable.** A ROM is a deterministic program; run it in an accurate emulator and you can observe exactly what it does. That changes the center of gravity entirely: the hard part here is not "is this true," it's "is this disassembly actually correct and actually verified," and the standard of rigor is a real emulation trace, not a falsification framework built around irreducible historical uncertainty. See [`methods/falsification-standard.md`](methods/falsification-standard.md) for how this project's evaluation standard reflects that.

## A hard legal/ethical boundary, from launch — never negotiable

Atari 2600 game ROMs are, in general, **still under copyright.** This project:

- **Never commits, bulk-downloads, or redistributes copyrighted ROM binaries in this repository, under any circumstance.**
- Limits analysis targets to: (a) ROMs in the public domain or released under an explicit open license by their rights holder (there is a real, active homebrew scene that does this), (b) ROM files the user supplies from their own legally obtained copies, used only for local analysis on the user's own machine and **never committed to or redistributed through this repository**, or (c) commentary and disassembly of material already extensively documented in the public reverse-engineering literature (the Stella emulator project, 6502.org, AtariAge's development community, published books such as *Racing the Beam*), cited rather than reproduced wholesale.
- See `config/sidequests.md` SQ-1 for the first task: scoping exactly which targets are legally clear before any disassembly work begins.

## How it works

**Roles** (`/agents/`) — each is a persona with a fixed mission statement and methodology, not a fixed conclusion:
- [`disassembler.md`](agents/disassembler.md) — the lead role: produces and verifies 6502/6507 opcode-level disassembly
- [`tia-specialist.md`](agents/tia-specialist.md) — the Television Interface Adaptor's cycle-exact video-timing model ("racing the beam") that nearly every game's rendering code depends on
- [`memory-cartographer.md`](agents/memory-cartographer.md) — maps the console's 128 bytes of RAM, RIOT I/O, and cartridge bank-switching schemes
- [`historian.md`](agents/historian.md) — catalogs existing public disassembly/documentation efforts and notable prior reverse-engineering findings, so this project builds on public knowledge instead of duplicating it
- [`skeptic.md`](agents/skeptic.md) — central role: no disassembly or memory-map claim is accepted without an actual emulation trace confirming it

**Operating configuration** (`/config/`) — reviewable instructions for the simulated research department, the lead agent's autonomous manager role, the auditor agent's non-blocking review role, compute use, and the sidequest queue.

**Knowledge base** (`/knowledge-base/state.md`) — the current shared state: confirmed, trace-verified findings; disassembly work in progress; and open questions. This file only changes via pull request, so every revision is a permanent, reviewable git commit.

**Logs** (`/logs/`) — append-only. One file per work session per agent. Never edited after creation.

**Data** (`/data/`) — disassembly outputs, memory maps, and trace logs for rights-clear ROMs only. No copyrighted ROM binaries are ever stored here.

**Comms** (`/comms/`) — how the two lead AIs talk to each other: [`FromClaudeToChatGPT.md`](comms/FromClaudeToChatGPT.md) and [`FromChatGPTToClaude.md`](comms/FromChatGPTToClaude.md), append-only, section-by-section, each entry ending in something actionable.

**Procedures** (`/procedures/`) — step-by-step checklists for tasks this project does repeatedly, written only after a real incident shows the informal version isn't reliable enough. Empty at launch by design.

**Promotion standard** — before a disassembly or memory-map claim becomes a Confirmed Finding, it must meet the repository's [evaluation standard](methods/falsification-standard.md): a reproducible emulation trace, not just a plausible reading of the bytes.

## Status

Bootstrap. This repository is a freshly scaffolded member of the research-collective family, carrying over the same governance framework, agent roles, comms protocol, and evidentiary discipline, adapted to verified software reverse-engineering instead of a historical text or artifact. No ROM has been analyzed yet, and the knowledge base starts empty. The first task is the toolchain setup and ROM-rights scoping (`config/sidequests.md`, SQ-1) — see `comms/FromClaudeToChatGPT.md` Round 1 for the concrete starting instruction.

## Public research site

Once live, the project record will be published from `docs/` the same way as the sibling projects' sites. See `.github/workflows/pages.yml`.
